item.title: Google Play Redesign Adapts to Car Displays (1 minute read)
item.description: Google's redesigned Play Store for cars with Google built-in adapts to different display sizes and orientations, rolling out automatically over the coming weeks. Entertainment collections for parked use sit apart from driving-related options, and a left-side rail becomes a top bar in portrait. YouTube Premium subscribers get background audio when the car shifts into drive, and Firefox and STARZ join the lineup.

item.title: Adobe Software Dupe Maker Takes on Microsoft Office, Releasing Free Versions of Word, PowerPoint, and Excel (2 minute read)
item.description: A developer who used AI to recreate Adobe's creative apps in Rust as free, open-source tools is now taking on Microsoft Office. WordCraft, DeckCraft, and GridCraft arrive as free stand-ins for Word, PowerPoint, and Excel under the ArtCraft brand. Some subreddits removed posts over cybersecurity and ethics concerns about AI-generated code. Supporters frame the apps as a protest against Adobe's subscription tactics.

item.title: Opera Air gets a minimalist makeover with a focus on distraction-free browsing (2 minute read)
item.description: Opera Air has been redesigned around distraction-free browsing, using a cleaner interface that keeps additional tools hidden until they are needed. New wallpapers use open spaces, perspective, and natural textures that adapt to light and dark themes, while built-in Soundscapes combine ambient sounds and original music to encourage focus or relaxation. The browser also includes customizable break reminders, breathing exercises, neck stretches, an ad blocker, and a free VPN while allowing messaging and social apps to remain accessible through the sidebar.

item.title: Critique in the AI Era (6 minute read)
item.description: AI can produce twelve credible variations before the coffee cools, so the design crit should become a debrief, like an F1 team studying telemetry over finishing position. Teams ask about reasoning, friction with the model and verification, and also critique the setup: briefs, constraints, and rubrics. AI critics tend to agree with the designer, and great AI-first designers sense limits, give precise feedback, and know when to override the model.

item.title: Scaling the Design Process (1 minute read)
item.description: Static personas capture real-world complexity poorly in intelligence-driven products, where outcomes are probabilistic and vary across people and contexts. AI lets teams build products that adapt to individual users at scale, which means designing for a spectrum of outcomes.

item.title: Agentic Systems Are the Future of Brands (8 minute read)
item.description: Traditional brand guidelines struggle when teams and AI agents must constantly make decisions that were never explicitly documented, causing otherwise competent work to gradually drift toward generic outcomes. Agentic brand systems can instead encode decisions about voice, color, typography, layout, components, and behavior into structured, machine-readable instructions that both humans and agents can apply directly. As AI dramatically increases the volume and speed of production, documenting not just what a brand looks like but why and how its decisions should be made becomes essential for maintaining coherence.

item.description: The Design Systems Directory catalogs more than 180 design systems, component libraries, and UI toolkits with filters for technology, industry, accessibility, Figma support, design tokens, AI guidance, MCP, skills, and llms.txt.

item.description: Recent Design is a curated platform that focuses on the latest trends in web, interface, and interaction design.

item.title: STUDIO HERRSTRÖM rebrands Sony Music imprint Milkshake (4 minute read)
item.description: Studio Herrström's identity for Sony Music imprint Milkshake combines references from car culture, flavored drinks, and pop music into a single energetic visual language. The original splash mark has been redrawn as a rounded emblem inspired by fluid, metal, and reflections, accompanied by neon pinks, high-vis yellows, asphalt blacks, soft lilacs, and the neo-grotesque Gates typeface. Information layouts borrow from car window permits and milk carton nutrition tables, creating structured containers for track titles, release dates, copyright information, and other details across digital and promotional materials.

item.title: Fit height to background pattern size with calc-size() (4 minute read)
item.description: CSS background patterns can end awkwardly when a container's content produces a height that isn't an exact multiple of the background tile, while `background-repeat: round` fixes the edge by distorting the pattern itself. Combining `calc-size()` with `round()` instead lets the browser calculate the element's natural height and round it up to the nearest multiple of the tile height. The result behaves similarly to `min-height`, preserving both the content-driven size and the original pattern proportions, though browser support remains limited.

item.title: How to Turn an AI-Generated Logo into a Professional Logo (10 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated logos work as starting concepts, not finished brand assets, and need real editing before professional use.

item.title: How Any Designer Can Build a More Open Design Culture at Work (5 minute read)
item.description: Designers at any level can build a more open design culture by creating psychological safety one conversation at a time.

item.title: Getty Images to go private after restructuring deal (1 minute read)
item.description: Getty Images is planning a prepackaged Chapter 11 filing and will go private, backed by up to $533 million from the Getty family and Koch Equity Development. The deal follows a collapsed $3.7 billion Shutterstock merger and leaves the company, carrying over $1.3 billion in debt, wholly family- and Koch-owned. Generative AI image tools keep squeezing the stock-licensing business of both Getty and Shutterstock.

item.title: AI Agent Developer Manus Raises $500M+ at Reported $4B Valuation (2 minute read)
item.description: Manus has raised more than $500 million in a round led by Boyu Capital, with Tencent participating, at a reported $4 billion valuation. That figure roughly doubles Meta's reported offer, an acquisition Chinese regulators blocked in April. The newly released Manus 2.0 cuts token use by 23.2% on some tasks and adds Cloud Computer and Cue.

item.title: iOS 27.2 beta 4 removes Apple's redesigned Health app and brings back the old design (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple has removed its redesigned Health app from iOS 27.2 beta 4, restoring the existing interface after allowing testers to try the overhaul in earlier betas. The redesign introduced features including Insights, Longevity, Health Age, and readiness metrics, but Apple had already indicated that it would arrive separately later in 2026. Data collected while testing the new version remains available through Settings, suggesting the redesign has been delayed rather than abandoned.

item.title: On what a clean interface hides (5 minute read)
item.description: Minimal interfaces can reduce visible complexity while quietly transferring more work to users, who must discover hidden controls, interpret ambiguous icons, and infer what happened after an action. Comparing a hidden bookmark icon with an explicit Save button demonstrates how adding labels, confirmation, and an Undo action can make an interface visually busier but cognitively simpler. Good interface design therefore requires balancing visual restraint with enough visible information to support newcomers, while potentially reducing that guidance as familiarity grows.

item.title: Emerging Patterns: Design Leadership in 2026 (15 minute read)
item.description: Research involving 119 design leaders found 93 distinct routes into the profession, with fewer than 30% having studied in dedicated design programs and nearly 40% beginning their careers elsewhere. Traditional career ladders are giving way to more diversified portfolio careers, while 94% of respondents expect their tool stacks to change dramatically over the next five years as AI transforms design work. The qualities that appear most durable amid this uncertainty are not technical skills but intuition, navigation, adaptability, resilience, and stewardship, including a growing commitment among established designers to mentor the next generation.

item.title: When code is no longer the constraint: Inside Anthropic's design team (12 minute read)
item.description: AI has accelerated engineering at Anthropic to the point where deciding what deserves to be built is becoming a greater constraint than implementing it, pushing designers closer to production code and working prototypes. Designers routinely build their own tools, generate interactive variations using Anthropic's design system, and collaborate through smaller, more frequent critiques and working demos rather than lengthy specifications. Technical fluency is increasingly useful, but Anthropic also values designers who continually reinvent their workflows, have a point of view about where software is heading, and can move fluidly between strategic direction and hands-on making.

item.description: Open Source UI components built on a design philosophy where every animation serves a functional purpose — motion is information, not decoration.

item.title: The Missing Foundation for AI-Generated Websites (Website)

item.title: Build Your Own Design Apps with AI (Website)
item.description: Toolcraft is an open-source starter kit and UI library for building custom design apps with AI. Use it to create branded asset generators, explore new visual styles, and turn repetitive design tasks into reusable tools.

item.title: Thumbnails Give a Fast Overview (15 minute read)
item.description: Thumbnails let people choose by looking rather than reading, because a scene's gist registers in about a tenth of a second. They fail when neighbors look identical or a preview misrepresents the click, so the two rules are: differ from your neighbors, and resemble your destination. Fourteen guidelines follow, along with the risks AI brings when it selects, personalizes, or synthesizes previews.

item.title: Experience Planes – The Big 4: Who, What, Where, and Why of Experiences (10 minute read)
item.description: Picking a single lens such as customer, shopping, or brand experience quietly shapes a design conversation before any design begins. Four experience planes widen the view: who is involved, what they are doing, where it happens, and why the organization offers it. Five examples, from license renewal to food delivery, show frustration often sitting in the connections between places.

item.title: How two simple dots gave Pictoplasma a fresh personality for 2026 (7 minute read)
item.description: andstudio transformed Pictoplasma's deliberately neutral identity around the positioning “Never faceless,” giving the character-design festival its own personality without competing with the work it showcases. A customized version of Lift Type's Melun adds a glyph containing two dots that function as eyes, allowing typography itself to become a character through pareidolia while colors and layouts change between festival editions. The same two-dot device extends into motion, print, installations, tattoos, and guerrilla applications, creating a playful system simple enough to work within the festival's limited budget.

item.title: André Britz draws dimly remembered landscapes, in a book held together with a pink elastic band (5 minute read)
item.description: André Britz's Gone with the Clouds collects intuitive landscapes drawn entirely from memory in a 64-page publication whose loose pages and pink elastic binding deliberately remain changeable, mirroring how memories blur, shift, and rearrange themselves over time.

item.title: The chaotic Apple HomeView ad is stressful viewing (4 minute read)
item.description: Apple's HomeView launch ad depicts a chaotic family morning, with the shared smart-home display handling messages, entertainment, and home controls.

This means that the differences that matter don't show up on a features page. They show up six months in.Vidmob built a 7-question rubric to cut through the sameness (plus a scorecard to compare vendors side by side). item.title: As They Supposedly Battle AI Slop, Major Publishers Reportedly Cover Their Books in It (2 minute read)
item.description: Three of the big five publishers reportedly use AI for cover art and publicity copy without telling authors or the public. Wired's report, drawn from more than two dozen anonymous employees, names tools including ChatGPT, Claude, and image generators. Leadership subscribes to AI tools and runs brainstorming sessions asking staff to find uses, even as the big five sue Meta over copyright.

item.title: Prize-Winning Image Which Sparked Backlash Was AI-Generated, Nikon Rules (2 minute read)
item.description: Nikon has disqualified the winning video of its Small World in Motion microscopy contest, ruling that generative AI used in its composition broke the rules. Scientists, including former judges, had flagged the footage of cilia in a child's airway as fake. The camera-maker is now reviewing the procedures of the annual contest, which has run for 15 years.

item.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm (2 minute read)
item.description: Facebook's new “Your Algorithm” feature lets users describe in their own words what they want to see more or less of in Feed and Reels, with Meta saying recommendations update in real time. An updated three-dot menu provides access to the tool alongside “Interested” and “Not interested” options, and Facebook may ask follow-up questions to understand users' feedback. The launch brings controls already introduced on Instagram to Facebook, giving users a more direct way to shape their recommendations.

item.title: The Fake Double Diamond is Dead. The Real Double Diamond is Immortal (6 minute read)
item.description: Synthetic users and AI-generated insights offer the false certainty of up-front discovery without its substance, and they never remove the need to iterate. Shipping everything and letting analytics decide fails too, because real experiments need a hypothesis, an end point, and cleanup of failed bets. The fake double diamond trades real divergence for synthetic urgency. Useful software needs problem definition and iteration in one shared system.

item.title: What are we willing to sacrifice for AI? (7 minute read)
item.description: If AI eventually allows companies to produce goods and services with far fewer workers, economies built around exchanging labor for income may face a fundamental contradiction. Three broad responses each demand a sacrifice: businesses could preserve jobs at the expense of potential profits, society could restrict AI and forgo some of its benefits, or economic systems could provide guaranteed income or broader ownership while accepting greater institutional dependence. The deeper question is whether existing ideas about liberty and economic independence can survive if meaningful opportunities to earn a living through work become scarce.

item.title: TypeType Unveils TT Rationalist Typography (3 minute read)
item.description: TypeType's updated TT Rationalist modernizes the slab serif with trapezoidal serifs, softer stroke contrast, humanist proportions, and curved details that make dense text feel less rigid and more comfortable to read. The family spans 22 styles, including ten upright weights, matching true italics, and two variable fonts, with 1,127 glyphs per style and 31 OpenType features. Support for more than 235 Latin- and Cyrillic-based languages makes the family flexible enough for everything from editorial layouts and cultural posters to apps, watch interfaces, and compact digital typography.

item.title: Fix the Contrast without Losing Your Brand (3 minute read)
item.description: Low-contrast text appears on 83.9% of the top million home pages, making it the web's most common accessibility failure. Clearleft's tool “This hue shall pass” maps every pairing in a palette against WCAG AA or AAA and fixes failures by nudging lightness. Hue stays fixed, so brand colors keep their character while passing contrast.

item.title: Pentagram creates dynamic bilingual identity for Design Doha Biennial 2026 (4 minute read)
item.description: Pentagram's identity for the 2026 Design Doha Biennial replaces a static logo with a flexible typographic system built around connectivity and equal treatment of Arabic and English. Extended strokes stretch between elements like mapping lines or network constellations, while regional travertine beige and deep maroon are combined with bright orange and the blue established by the inaugural edition. The same structural logic extends across sub-brands and exhibitions, allowing individual programs to develop distinct expressions while remaining part of a coherent bilingual system.

item.title: A' Design Award Winners Achieve Real World Impact through Graphic Design (6 minute read)
item.description: A curated selection of 2026 A' Design Award winners shows graphic design and packaging delivering real-world impact, including Gold winners Aisling Sans and Dotline Corporate Identity.

item.title: The Best Way to Use Icons in Web UIs (18 minute read)
item.description: Icons can be inserted and swapped from CSS alone by storing them as custom-property design tokens and rendering them through masked pseudo-elements.

item.title: Google Debuts SynthID Detector Tool for Flagging AI-Generated Content, but It's Far from Perfect (3 minute read)
item.description: Google's new web-based SynthID Detector opens AI-content checks to anyone who signs in, flagging images, video, and audio from Google, OpenAI, Nvidia, or Kakao models. It misses AI content without a SynthID watermark, such as output from Claude, Grok, and Chinese open-weights models, and cannot tell fully generated media from AI-edited media. Without a universal watermarking standard across all major model makers, a reliable way to detect AI content likely will never exist.

item.title: Smoother Design Collaboration and Navigation on Figma's Mobile App (1 minute read)
item.description: Smoother collaboration and navigation arrive in Figma's mobile app through a page dropdown, a frame preview slider, and share links to the exact page or frame. Individual frames and images export to the phone with format and size options, and the app reopens exactly where users left off.

item.title: iPhone Air 2 is coming, here's everything we know so far (3 minute read)
item.description: Apple's second-generation iPhone Air is reportedly coming in spring 2027 with upgrades aimed at addressing several compromises of the ultra-thin original. A second rear ultra-wide camera will join the main camera, while a larger 3,500mAh battery and more efficient 2nm A20 Pro chip should improve battery life. Apple is also expected to add vapor chamber cooling, allowing the thin device to stay cooler and sustain performance for longer.

item.title: On Being Anything Other Than a Designer (4 minute read)
item.description: A year of trying to be anything other than a designer comes as the AI era proves unkind to human-centered designers, especially outside massive companies. Every company has people who absorb organizational mess, work that pays poorly, carries no title, and is sometimes called glue work. The answer is not another heroic generalist but building enough capability into teams to understand customer need, experiment technically, and stop solving problems twice.

item.title: POV: AI needs mascots, and only humans can make them (8 minute read)
item.description: AI companies are increasingly turning abstract technology into approachable characters, with mascots such as Muse, Dots, Claw'd, and Notion's animated face giving unfamiliar systems personalities people can understand and relate to. Anthropomorphism satisfies human desires for connection and predictability, while animation can turn a few simple shapes into a character that appears to think, hesitate, search, greet, and react. The strongest mascots become storytelling systems rather than logos with arms, requiring human skills such as observation, empathy, timing, humor, restraint, and a coherent sense of personality.

item.title: The Convergence of Design (2 minute read)
item.description: Products often converge toward similar forms as their purpose becomes clearer, technologies mature, and physical constraints, economics, standards, and competition narrow the range of practical designs. Software can converge even faster, as demonstrated by the rapid spread of chat interfaces following ChatGPT, while emerging AI hardware remains in an experimental phase of pins, glasses, earbuds, and pendants. Whether through functional optimization, market pressures, shared constraints, or simple imitation, successful forms tend to become increasingly alike until a change in purpose or technology opens new possibilities.

item.title: Jev for Designers (3 minute read)
item.description: TypeSafe's Jev answers choice, score, and yes-or-no questions with a probability for each option instead of writing text. Its training rewards honest probabilities over confident-sounding answers, giving designers the calibrated uncertainty design work needs, though it reads only text and takes questions literally. A new demo adds a maybe zone to HeyStefan's emoji sorter, where Jev parks undecided emoji from a pile of 166.

item.title: Louise Laborie draws the lonely, cinematic and in-between parts of America (4 minute read)
item.description: French illustrator Louise Laborie uses watercolor and charcoal to depict America's motels, highways, skate parks, and other transitional spaces at dusk, populating them with teenagers caught between childhood and adulthood to create quiet, cinematic scenes shaped by loneliness, music, memory, and imagined stories.

item.title: 2026 is the Year of the Canceled Ad (4 minute read)
item.description: 2026 became the year of the canceled ad, with Pepsi, Novig, Oxford United, Converse, and a golf brand facing backlash, some by accident and some by design.

item.title: Digital Artist Turns Photo Manipulation and Digital Painting into Cosmic Sanctuaries of Solitude and Wonder (1 minute read)
item.description: CriS Cian turns photo manipulation and digital painting into peaceful, poetic cosmic scenes of futuristic expeditions and encounters beyond Earth.

item.title: The new Apple TV could have a built-in mic and a remote with a speaker (1 minute read)
item.description: Apple's next Apple TV will reportedly include a microphone for hands-free Siri commands, letting users control playback and smart-home devices without reaching for the remote. A speaker in the redesigned remote could sound an alert to help locate it when misplaced. The refresh is also expected to feature an A19 chip supporting Siri AI and begin shipping October 30 alongside an updated HomePod Mini.

item.title: Google's New Playground Aims to Make It Easy to Vibe Code a Game Right in Your Browser (2 minute read)
item.description: Google launched Playground, a browser-based platform where anyone can build and share games by chatting with AI, with no coding experience required. Powered by Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria, it lets users keep refining a game, then keep it private or publish it to the Explore gallery. Playground launched free in the US for users 18 and older, with Google One AI subscribers getting early access to creation and a higher token limit.

item.title: Gamma Revamps Presentation Platform to Make Output Look More Human (4 minute read)
item.description: Gamma 5 rebuilds the presentation platform with a redesigned editor, a more capable AI agent, and more visual styles to fight the "AI smell" of repetitive layouts. The agent works in a sandbox with automated layout checks, while about 20 connectors pull in sources such as Slack and Granola. Co-founder Jon Noronha says some users cut presentation time from eight to 10 hours down to about 30 minutes.

item.title: First AI came and scooped up your art. Now it's scooped up Adobe (4 minute read)
item.description: ArtCraft is a two-person GitHub project that appears to use AI-generated code to recreate large parts of Adobe's Creative Cloud functionality, including alternatives to Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Lightroom, and Premiere. Its rapid development demonstrates how AI coding tools could allow tiny teams to reproduce increasingly sophisticated professional software that previously required huge organizations to build. The development creates an ironic reversal for Adobe, whose own embrace of generative AI has faced criticism from creatives concerned about AI systems reproducing their work.

item.title: The New Big Ball of Mud: Why Agentic AI Systems Turn Fragile (12 minute read)
item.description: With AI making building nearly free, vibe architects without technical backgrounds grow agentic systems piecemeal into fragile "big balls of mud." Study participants kept throwaway drafts, bolted-on features, and let the AI patch files until they could no longer locate or recreate their own systems. Keeping global, local, and ambient context separate lets builders direct a rebuild instead of relying on the AI as sole navigator.

item.title: Handle Token Exceptions (5 minute read)
item.description: Hardcoded values become valid token exceptions only with a reason, a defined scope, an owner, and an end date. Without a date, they're permanent technical debt. Valid cases include time-boxed campaigns, tokens awaiting release, and urgent accessibility fixes. A register tracks each exception's location, value, reason, approver, and expiration date, and when the date arrives, it's promoted to a token or removed.

item.title: Designing Michelangelus (8 minute read)
item.description: Michelangelus is a new serif typeface inspired by Michelangelo's handwritten manuscripts, architectural work, and carved inscriptions, created by Studiogusto for the 400th anniversary of the consecration of St. Peter's Basilica. Rather than reproducing his handwriting literally, the designers studied its rhythm, spacing, proportions, distinctive forms, and hidden structural order, even spending a week refining the lowercase “g” derived from his signature. The resulting family contains more than 2,000 glyphs across regular, italic, bold, and bold italic styles and will become available across Microsoft 365 later this year.

item.title: On giving fluid interfaces an anchor (6 minute read)
item.description: Interfaces that continuously reshape themselves in response to context, AI, or user intent risk becoming difficult to understand because people lose the stable landmarks they use to build a mental model of a product. Keeping frequently used action buttons anchored while content expands gives users a predictable place to click or tap as the interface changes. Fluid interfaces therefore work best when adaptability is balanced with enough permanence for users to understand where they are, what changed, and how to get back.

item.title: Why Icon Consistency is Harder Than It Looks (5 minute read)
item.description: Ten small decisions, from stroke weight and spacing to perspective and optical corrections, keep the thousandth icon in a set looking drawn by the same hand. Expressive styles bring more rules and more room for inconsistency. When strict rules hurt recognition, legibility wins, which is why the Sharp style keeps a few curves.

item.title: Its embroidered logo invite shows Apple understands something other tech brands don't (4 minute read)
item.description: Apple's hand-embroidered rainbow logo for its Welcome Home event continues a shift toward visibly human-made advertising, using behind-the-scenes craft as part of the brand message at a time when audiences are increasingly skeptical of AI-generated creative work.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV Condemns AI Art and Defends the Importance of Human Creativity (2 minute read)
item.description: Pope Leo XIV condemned AI art in a Vatican speech, arguing that algorithms lack the "spark" of the human.

item.title: Fanta's AI Slop Halloween Ad is a Real Horror Show (2 minute read)
item.description: Fanta's AI-generated "Haunted Universe" Halloween ad, made by studio GRAiL, drew almost entirely negative comments, with some viewers vowing never to buy Fanta again.

item.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface (2 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Intelligent UI lets ChatGPT combine text with interactive diagrams, charts, buttons, and task-specific tools instead of using the same format for every answer. Users can explore explanations, change inputs, or use a calculator directly within a conversation, with the layout adapting to the question. The feature is rolling out with GPT-6 across paid and free plans, and users can reduce visual elements when they prefer simpler responses.

item.title: Google Releases Nano Banana 2.1 for Image Generation and Editing (1 minute read)
item.description: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 reached the Gemini API for image generation and editing, at 1K, 2K, and 4K resolutions. Google reports better text rendering, prompt adherence, and character consistency across successive edits, plus fixes for tiling artifacts in wide and panoramic images at 2K and 4K. The model is available as gemini-nano-banana-2.1, and Google has deprecated gemini-3.1-flash-image without announcing a shutdown date.

item.title: ChatGPT can imitate a cartoonist. Now it's signing their name, too (3 minute read)
item.description: ChatGPT has generated cartoons containing signatures associated with more than 15 New Yorker contributors, potentially making AI-generated work appear to have been created by real artists. Cartoonists including Brendan Loper and Emily Flake have encountered images bearing recognizable versions of their names despite having no involvement in creating them. OpenAI has introduced warnings for some New Yorker-style requests, but signed outputs have reportedly continued to appear, raising concerns that style imitation can cross into false attribution.

item.title: Imperfection (5 minute read)
item.description: A personal website redesign became an excuse to explore deliberately playful details, including fake game cartridges for past jobs, draggable photo prints, paper-like shaders, animated labels, unusual links, and dynamically generated social cards. Many of these touches serve little practical purpose, but that lack of optimization is precisely what makes the process enjoyable and gives the site its personality. Personal projects can create space for experimentation that professional work often removes, making unnecessary details, imperfection, and prolonged tinkering valuable in themselves.

item.title: Slack Content Design in the Age of AI (8 minute read)
item.description: Slack's AI-drafted UI copy is almost indistinguishable from human work, and content designers are uniquely equipped to close the trust gap that "almost" opens. When Slackbot appeared to leak private information that was actually hallucinated, the team redesigned the UX to fetch correct data and explain why LLMs hallucinate. Three tenets guide the work: trust is the product, human judgment is irreplaceable, and language is infrastructure for AI agents.

item.title: Building a General-Purpose Accessibility Agent—and What We Learned in the Process (11 minute read)
item.description: An experimental general-purpose accessibility agent piloted at GitHub has reviewed 3,535 pull requests with a 68% resolution rate. It gives engineers real-time guidance in Copilot CLI and VS Code, and fixes straightforward issues before code reaches production. A parent agent directs two sub-agents, a passive reviewer and an active implementer, and escalates drag-and-drop, data grids, and rich text editors to human specialists.

item.description: A Safari extension for Mac that measures any website's colors, type, spacing, and layout, then hands it to your coding agent as one measured prompt.

item.title: Energy Icons — energy transition icons (Website)
item.description: Energy Icons is an open-source library of more than 1,200 icons for energy and climate products, covering areas such as renewables, electricity, transportation, buildings, and decarbonization in two optical sizes and two weights.

item.description: Create physical products with Autonomyware: everyday objects, complex systems, sculpts, and toys, engineered autonomously from your idea.

item.title: Testing the iPad Air M4 as a multi-disciplinary artist: does it stack up? (7 minute read)
item.description: The M4 iPad Air's 12GB of unified memory brings it much closer to the iPad Pro for demanding creative work, comfortably handling large Procreate files, 3D models approaching 20 million polygons, and ProRes video editing. Its M4 chip delivers roughly 42% higher single-core and 44% higher multi-core Geekbench performance than the M2 Air, while Apple Pencil Pro support provides the same drawing experience as higher-end models. The iPad Pro still offers advantages such as an OLED display, nano-texture glass, and more memory, but many artists, illustrators, 3D artists, photographers, and video editors may no longer need to pay the premium.

item.title: Mother Design exercises restraint with new M&S pack system (5 minute read)
item.description: Mother Design has created a restrained packaging system for thousands of M&S Home and Lingerie products by removing competing sub-brands and hierarchies and looking to classic information design rather than other retailers for inspiration. The system standardizes MS London typography, introduces a geometric numeral set called MS London Geo, and uses grids, consistent hierarchy, restrained colors, and color-coded sizing to make complex product information easier to navigate. Packaging materials, photography, and tone adapt between Home and Lingerie while maintaining a shared structure designed to strengthen the M&S master brand and scale into additional categories.

item.title: Pinterest's AI Now Turns Beauty Pins into Action Plans (1 minute read)
item.description: Pinterest's AI-powered Beauty Guides turn saved hair and nail Pins into action plans to take to the salon. Tapping "Get the Guide" translates a look into stylist terms like "balayage," "root melt," and "almond nails," plus the time, price range, and maintenance involved. At launch, the feature covers Pins for hairstyle, color, nail shape, and finish.

item.description: The Figma agent is generally available, leaving beta with improved latency, in-chat file search, and configurable guidelines that give it context about design libraries. Teammates' agents can be watched live on the canvas, generative plugins reach general availability, and custom skills arrive on Starter.

item.title: Leaked images reveal Apple's new Home smart lock, thermostat, more for LG (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple has reportedly co-developed a collection of smart home accessories with LG, including a smart lock, thermostat, temperature sensor, video doorbell, and several security cameras. Leaked images show a deadbolt with a rotating keypad and automatic unlocking alongside the thermostat and temperature sensor. The accessories will carry LG branding and are unlikely to ship alongside Apple's imminent Home product launches, but they could still feature in the company's announcements.

item.title: Why I Wait for Research to Prove Something is Needed before It's Added to the UI (3 minute read)
item.description: Adding indicators for annotated documents to a collapsed accordion was set aside until research shows users need them, since more on-screen information raises cognitive load. Adding the element first obscures the cause, since a user who ignores it may not have needed it, barely benefited, or never seen it. Seeing users repeatedly expand documents to find annotations would be the clear signal to add indicators.

item.title: What does “good enough” actually mean for designers now? (5 minute read)
item.description: AI has raised expectations for speed and visual polish, creating a “fidelity trap” where designers feel pressure to make every artifact look finished even when rougher work would better support the decision at hand. A practical definition of “good enough” starts by identifying what the work needs to unlock—such as a usability test, engineering estimate, design direction, or leadership approval—and applying only enough fidelity to achieve that goal. Clear quality criteria can help teams know both when work isn't ready and when to stop, preserving human judgment as AI compresses more of the design process.

item.title: Why Granola's Lack of Onboarding Backfires When You Test It (7 minute read)
item.description: People trying an AI note-taking app for the first time are likely to record a meaningless test before trusting it with a real meeting, yet Granola's mobile experience provides little reassurance that the recording is working. Instead of trying to change this instinctive behavior, Granola could embrace it with a one-time test mode that shows a live transcript or otherwise demonstrates the product's capabilities before normal use. Features designed to appear only once can still be valuable because the first session disproportionately shapes perception, particularly in a crowded category where users can easily try a competitor.

item.title: Beyond Productivity: Designing Space for Creativity (8 minute read)
item.description: Creativity dies from overload, not laziness, so a Reset, Spark, and Protect framework builds in breaks, joy, and boundaries with technology. Breaks of 20 to 30 minutes, walks, time in nature, and naps restore the brain, and AI works best as a calculator, not a composer. Joy is designed through paid sabbaticals, company-wide shutdowns, and permission to be a beginner, while switching off notifications guards attention.

item.title: More than a mark (5 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft redesigned Copilot's icon around two simple square-derived forms that combine into one silhouette, creating a mark capable of remaining recognizable while moving and changing across contexts. Color retains a connection to Copilot's original gradient, while a motion language turns the icon into part of the interface by visually communicating when Copilot is thinking, planning, or retrieving information. The same behaviors follow users across Windows, Word, PowerPoint, and other experiences, transforming a static brand asset into a functional part of how the product communicates.

item.title: Jaguar's controversial rebrand finally makes sense with the unveiling of the bold Type 01 (4 minute read)
item.description: Jaguar's Type 01 production EV reveals how its controversial 2024 rebrand anticipated an intentionally polarizing product strategy rather than simply introducing a new visual identity. The dramatic 1,015-horsepower electric grand tourer was designed before the Type 00 concept, which was reverse-engineered and exaggerated to generate attention, while consumer testing produced unusually high numbers of both very low and very high ratings. By abandoning the middle ground, Jaguar is targeting wealthy, design-focused buyers who want something distinctive rather than trying to retain its traditional executive-car audience.

item.description: Real-world comparisons between the iPhone 18 Pro's f/1.48 and f/1.8 apertures show a subtle but useful increase in natural background blur and subject separation without relying on computational Portrait mode.

item.title: Photoshop's Controversial New AI Tool is Dividing Opinion (3 minute read)
